texts.facts: These three appeals are directed against the common order dated 04.12.2014( hereinafter referred to as "impugned order") canvassing a common question of law and facts and as such, it would be appropriate to dispose them of by a single judgment. 2. All the three appeals are directed against the impugned order passed by Sh. Vivek Kumar Tripathi, Ld. Adjudicating Officer/ADM (New Delhi), Govt. of NCT of Delhi whereby penalty of Rs.2,50,000/ each was imposed upon M/s FSAT Appeal Nos.1/15, 2/15 &3/15 Page No.2 of 14 A.L.Chowdhary & Company,Supplier/ Distributer Firm(appellant in appeal no.2/15) & M/s The Claridges Hotel, Food Business Operator(appellant in appeal no. 3/15) whereas Rs.3,00,000/ was imposed upon manufacturing firm M/s Morde Foods Pvt. Ltd.(appellant in appeal no.1/15) praying therein; to [LEAKAGE_MASK] the impugned order. 3. The appeals were admitted for hearing. Notices of all these appeals were given to the respective respondents who have resisted the same. TCR was requisitioned. 4. The case of the prosecution, in brief is that on 12.10.2011 at about 4pm, Food Safety Officer Sh.Bal Mukand picked up four packets of 500grams each as sample of 'dark compound chocolate' from Sh.Neeraj Kumar Tyagi s/o Sh. Som Prakash Tyagi from the premises of M/s The Claridges Hotel (a unit of M/s Claridges Hotel Pvt.Ltd.), 12 Aurangzeb Road, New Delhi for analysis under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act(Packaging & Labeling) Regulations, 2011 ( hereinafter referred to as "FSSRs"). The said food article was found stored for human consumption at the time of taking sample from the said hotel. The rest of the formalities were also conducted. The Food Analyst analyzed the sample and found it to be misbranded vide report bearing No.PFA/Enf/585/2011 dated 18.10.2011 mentioning therein that the sample is misbranded because there is violation of regulation no.2.2.2.3 of the FSSRs as the label of the food article was found to be without declaration of nutritional information. Fsat Appeal No.1/15 vs Sh.Bal Mukand on 9 September, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29625161/ 2 FSAT Appeal Nos.1/15, 2/15 &3/15 Page No.3 of 14 5.
texts.arguments: 6. Feeling aggrieved, all the appellants have challenged the impugned order mainly on the grounds that the Ld. Adjudicating Officer did not conduct a fair inquiry and thus, he had erred to convict the appellants by imposing the penalty as detailed in paragraph 2 of the judgment. Secondly; the Ld. Adjudicating Officer had failed to appreciate the facts that the appellant M/s The Claridges Hotel was Food Business Operator (FBO) from whom four packets of 'dark compound chocolate' was picked up by the FSO in the same sealed condition as received/purchased from M/s Morde Foods Pvt. Ltd. ( Manufacturing Firm) through appellant/distributor M/s A. L. Chowdhary & Company who was neither the manufacturer nor the packer of the sampled commodity and thus, the defence of due diligence should have been extended to them and as such, they were liable to be protected by the warranty of M/s Morde Foods Pvt.Ltd. as provided in Section 80 (B)(2)(d)(i) of the FSS Act, 2006. Thirdly, the Ld. Adjudicating Officer had failed to appreciate that an item of packaged food which is ready for personal consumption by persons or families would cease to be pre packaged or pre packed food if purchased by an industrial consumer. To support his contentions, he has placed reliance upon the following judgment: Danisco(India) Private Limited Vs. Union of India and another,2014(2) FAC 109 wherein His Lordship was pleased to make the following observations: Important Point Packaging and Labelling Regulationsno objection certificate FSAT Appeal Nos.1/15, 2/15 &3/15 Page No.4 of 14 the safety of the product cannot be assessed without knowing mandatory labelling requirement prescribed under the Labelling Regulations and Guidelines issued by FSSAI the FSSAI is directed to examine the goods in question and issue a Noobjection certificate within a period of 10 days from today. Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011 noncompliance ofno objection certificaterefusing to grant the present petition has been filed by the petitioner seeking quashing of an email/communication dated 22.04.2014 of Technical Officer, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India whereby the petitioner's appeal, challenging the order refusing to grant a Noobjection certificate(NOC) to the consignment imported by the petitioner, was rejected on the ground that the said consignment did not comply with the requirements prescribed under the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011. The petitioner has also sought a direction to respondent no.2 to issue a Noobjection certificate(NOC) to the petitionerthe inspection/analysis of the consignment was carried out on 20.02.2014 and it was found that 'List of Ingredients' was not mentioned on the label the safety of the product cannot be assessed without knowing mandatory labelling requirement prescribed under the Labelling Regulations and Guidelines issued by FSSAI. The FSSAI also sent a rejection report dated 21.02.2014 to the Deputy Commissioner of Customs whether Regulation 2.2.2:2 of the Labelling Regulations is applicable, in entirety, to the goods imported by the petitioner. And, whether the labelling on the said goods is compliant with the statutory requirements of the FSS Act nutritional information is in any event inapplicable as the goods in question are lactic cultures which are to be used in manufacture of Fsat Appeal No.1/15 vs Sh.Bal Mukand on 9 September, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29625161/ 3 yoghurt. The goods in question being for industrial use, the logo indicating whether the goods are vegetarian or nonvegetarian is also ex facie inapplicableit is apparent that even though the Regulation 2.2.2:2 of the Labelling Regulations is not applicable, the labelling of the goods in question provides sufficient information. In addition, the petitioner has also furnished the detailed product description of the goods and FSAT Appeal Nos.1/15, 2/15 &3/15 Page No.5 of 14 has also specifically provided the composition, properties, physical/chemical specifications as well as microbiological specifications the impugned communication is [LEAKAGE_MASK] and the FSSAI is directed to examine the goods in question and issue a Noobjection certificate within a period of 10 days from today, if the goods are found to be in conformity with their description as available on the package, as well as the product description sheet provided by the petitioner. 7. Per contra, the Ld. Special PP has refuted the entire line of arguments whilst making submissions that the FBO firm was found storing misbranded food which did not contain any nutritional information being a food item meant for human consumption. They cannot claim any defence that only supplier and manufacturer are liable as they too carry out such mandatory checks of the food concerned being used for human consumption in any preparatory form. It needs to be noticed that the sampled article was kept for human consumption which is opined to be misbranded by the Public Analyst because of violation of Regulation No.2.2.2.3. of the FSSRs and as such, it comes within the mischief of Section 26 (2)(ii) of the FSS Act read with Section 3(1)(zf)( C)(i) of FSS Act which is punishable u/s 52 of the FSS Act. 8. First and foremost point raised by the Ld. Counsels for the appellants is that appellant M/s A.L.Chowdhary & Company, a partnership firm is engaged in distribution of cocoa products like dark compound chocolate manufactured by M/s Morde Foods Pvt. Ltd. The food article is sold in bulk packages to be used as raw material / intermediate product / ingredient by industries/institutions like hotels, air lines & other companies who may use it to manufacture other bakery and FSAT Appeal Nos.1/15, 2/15 &3/15 Page No.6 of 14 confectionery items etc. which was not for sale directly to the consumer in the same form. The sampled food article could be used only under controlled temperatures by processing/melting by the skilled/expert employees of the industries for its proper usages to make their own end product. As per the Public Analyst Report, the sampled food article was not found adulterated but the same was opined to be misbranded on account of non declaring the nutritional information on the label of the packages. It is further argued that nutritional information is not required to be mentioned on the packages of the food articles which are not meant for direct consumption by consumers. As the sampled commodity was to be used as raw material / intermediate product needed by industries to make their own end product and as such, the impugned order is not sustainable under the law. 9. Section 2 (ix) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 describes 'misbranding' of an article of food. The relevant clause 'k' relating to label reads as under : "2(ix) misbranded an article of food shall be deemed to be misbranded - (a) to (j)..... (k) If it is not labeled in accordance with the requirements of this Act or Rules made thereunder". Fsat Appeal No.1/15 vs Sh.Bal Mukand on 9 September, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29625161/ 4 10. In the matter of Danisco (India) Private Ltd. Vs Union of India and another(supra), His Lordships has quoted the relevant provisions of prepackaged food or prepacked food to deal with the controversy in question and the same are FSAT Appeal Nos.1/15, 2/15 &3/15 Page No.7 of 14 reproduced as under : "18. In addition to the General Labelling requirements specified in 2.2.1 above every package of food shall carry the following information on the label, namely, 1. The Name of Food: The name of the food shall include trade name or description of food contained in the package. 2. List of Ingredients: Except for single ingredient foods, a list of ingredients shall be declared on the label in the following manner: (a) The list of ingredients shall contain an appropriate title, such as the term "Ingredients"; (b) The name of Ingredients used in the product shall be listed in descending order of their composition by weight or volume, as the case may be, at the time of its manufacture; (c) A specific name shall be used for ingredients in the list of Ingredients:...." 19. The said Regulation reads as under: "8. "Prepackaged" or "Prepacked food", means food, which is placed in a package of any nature, in such a manner that the contents cannot be changed without tampering it and which is ready for sale to the consumer; Note: The expression "package" wherever it FSAT Appeal Nos.1/15, 2/15 &3/15 Page No.8 of 14 occurs in these Regulations, shall be construed as package containing pre packed food articles." 20. The expression 'consumer' has not been defined under the Labelling Regulations but is defined under Section 3(1)(f) of the FSS Act as under: "(f) "consumer" means persons and families purchasing and receiving food in order to meet their personal needs;" 21. (d) in the case of an offence involving the sale of food, that-- (i)The person sold the food in the same condition as and when the person purchased it.
